revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Real Estate
revealWordProblem.text: Terrance is helping his grandmother sell her house. He uses a real estate website to look at the recent sale prices of similarly‑sized houses in their area and collects the prices in the table shown. What would be a fair, but competitive, selling price for Terrance’s grandmother’s house? Use the median to justify your answer.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Sort the 16 sale prices from least to greatest: $160,000, $199,900, $239,900, $269,900, $307,000, $382,900, $385,400, $401,785, $402,400, $405,400, $423,400, $426,400, $454,400, $457,400, $460,400, $485,250. With 16 values (an even number), the median is the average of the 8th and 9th values: ($401,785 + $402,400) ÷ 2 = $804,185 ÷ 2 = $402,092.50. A fair, competitive selling price would be around $402,000, since that's the middle of the market and isn't pulled up or down by the lowest sale ($160,000) or the highest sale ($485,250).

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — What are mean, median, and mode?
conceptIntro.intro: Mean, median, and mode are three ways to find the center, or "typical" value, of a data set. The mean is the average, the median is the middle, and the mode is the most common value. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: The median is the middle value once the data is in order. With an even count, it is the mean of the two middle values — and it is the measure that an unusually high or low value cannot drag around.

iDo.title: Watch me find the median
lines: My data set: 2, 4, 4, 6, 9 — five values, already in order. Ordering first is what makes a middle exist at all.
With 5 values, the middle is the 3rd one. Counting in from both ends: 2 and 9 pair off, 4 and 6 pair off, and 4 is left alone.
So the median is 4. Half the values sit at or below it and half at or above it.
Now an even set: 2, 4, 6, 9. There is no single middle, so I take the mean of the two middle values: (4 + 6) ÷ 2 = 5. The median is 5, even though 5 is not in the data.

weDo.title: Let's do one together
lines: New data set, out of order: 13, 3, 7, 10, 7. Put it in order first.
In order: 3, 7, 7, 10, 13. Five values, so the middle is the 3rd.
The median is 7. Say what it means: a typical value in this set is about 7.
Now change the 13 to 130. Does the median move? It does not — still 7. That resistance is exactly why the median is used.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

youDo.title: Now you try — with support
lines: Try the practice problems below. The hint button is right there whenever you get stuck — use it, that's smart.

Remember the key idea: The median is the middle value once the data is in order. With an even count, it is the mean of the two middle values — and it is the measure that an unusually high or low value cannot drag around..

choiceFeedback: Add the numbers first—does 14 equal the sum divided by 5?
Did you forget to divide by the count of numbers?
Is 60 the mean, or the sum?
hints: Mean means the average of all five numbers — you'll need both a total and how many numbers there are.
Use the formula: mean = sum of the values ÷ how many values. Count first: there are 5 numbers here.
Step 1: add 10 + 14 + 8 + 12 + 16 to get the total. Then divide that total by 5 — the result is the mean.
hintsEs: La media es el promedio de los cinco números: necesitarás tanto un total como cuántos números hay.
Usa la fórmula: media = suma de los valores ÷ cuántos valores hay. Cuenta primero: aquí hay 5 números.
Paso 1: suma 10 + 14 + 8 + 12 + 16 para obtener el total. Luego divide ese total entre 5: el resultado es la media.

choiceFeedback: Did you order them first? What's the middle value after ordering?
The lowest is 3—is median always the lowest?
7 is not the middle value—order them first.
hints: Median = the middle number, but only AFTER the list is in order. Don't pick the middle of the unsorted list.
Rewrite 3, 7, 2, 9, 5 from least to greatest, then count in from both ends until you reach the one value in the exact middle.
Start ordering: the smallest is 2, then 3... finish the ordered list of all five values, then circle the 3rd one — that's the median.
approaching.explanationEs: Ordenados: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9. El valor del medio es 5.
hintsEs: La mediana es el número del medio, pero solo DESPUÉS de ordenar la lista. No elijas el del medio de la lista sin ordenar.
Reescribe 3, 7, 2, 9, 5 de menor a mayor y luego cuenta desde ambos extremos hasta llegar al único valor que queda justo en el medio.
Empieza a ordenar: el menor es 2, luego 3… termina la lista ordenada de los cinco valores y luego encierra el 3.º: esa es la mediana.

approaching.explanation: 4 appears three times — more than any other value. Mode = 4.
choiceFeedback: 7 appears once—which number appears most often?
9 appears once—count how many times each number shows up.
2 appears once—is mode the smallest or most frequent?
hints: Mode is about repeats — which value shows up in the list more times than any other?
Make a quick tally: write each different number and count how many times it appears in 4, 7, 4, 9, 2, 4, 8.
Start your tally: 7 appears once, 9 appears once... keep counting every number and pick the one with the highest tally.
approaching.explanationEs: El 4 aparece tres veces, más que cualquier otro valor. Moda = 4.
hintsEs: La moda tiene que ver con repeticiones: ¿qué valor aparece en la lista más veces que cualquier otro?
Haz un conteo rápido: escribe cada número distinto y cuenta cuántas veces aparece en 4, 7, 4, 9, 2, 4, 8.
Empieza tu conteo: el 7 aparece una vez, el 9 aparece una vez… sigue contando cada número y elige el de mayor conteo.

choiceFeedback: Add them up first, then divide by 5—not just multiply.
Count the numbers (5)—divide the sum by 5.
This is the sum—is sum the same as mean?
hints: Watch out: one tempting answer is just the total of the list. The mean asks you to go one step further.
Mean = total ÷ count. There are 5 values in this list, so after adding you must divide by 5.
Step 1: add 6 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 14. Step 2: take that total and divide it by 5. The quotient is your mean.
hintsEs: Cuidado: una respuesta tentadora es solo el total de la lista. La media te pide dar un paso más.
Media = total ÷ cantidad. Hay 5 valores en esta lista, así que después de sumar debes dividir entre 5.
Paso 1: suma 6 + 8 + 10 + 12 + 14. Paso 2: toma ese total y divídelo entre 5. El cociente es tu media.

approaching.title: The Mean Mistake (forgot to divide)

workedExample.label: Data set
workedExample.work: A player scored 6, 8, 10, and 6 points in 4 games.
workedExample.workEs: Un jugador anotó 6, 8, 10 y 6 puntos en 4 partidos.

workedExample.label: Goal
workedExample.work: Find the MEAN number of points.
workedExample.workEs: Encuentra la MEDIA de los puntos.

approaching.correctWork: Adding is only half of the mean. After adding (sum = 30) you must DIVIDE by how many values there are: 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5. The mean is 7.5 points, not 30.
hints: Mean = add then DIVIDE. The total of 30 is just the sum, not the mean.
There are 4 values, so divide the sum by 4: 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5.
approaching.titleEs: El error de la media (olvidó dividir)
approaching.explanation: The sum 6 + 8 + 10 + 6 = 30 is correct, but the answer stops there. The mean shares the total evenly across all the games, so you divide by the 4 values: 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5 points. A mean of 30 is also impossible here, since no single game reached 30 points.
approaching.explanationEs: La suma 6 + 8 + 10 + 6 = 30 está bien, pero la respuesta se detiene ahí. La media reparte el total en partes iguales entre todos los juegos, así que se divide entre los 4 valores: 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5 puntos. Una media de 30 también sería imposible aquí, porque ningún juego llegó a 30 puntos.
approaching.correctWorkEs: Sumar es solo la mitad de la media. Después de sumar (suma = 30) debes DIVIDIR entre cuántos valores hay: 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5. La media es 7.5 puntos, no 30.
hintsEs: Media = sumar y luego DIVIDIR. El total de 30 es solo la suma, no la media.
Hay 4 valores, así que divide la suma entre 4: 30 ÷ 4 = 7.5.

approaching.stem: Data set: 4, 6, 6, 8, 10, 12. What is the median?
approaching.explanation: With 6 values, the median is the average of the 3rd and 4th values: (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.
choiceFeedback: With an even count, take the average of the two middle values.
The two middle values are 6 and 8—what's their average?
Don't add all values and divide—find the middle two values.
hints: Count the values: there are 6, an even number — so no single value sits exactly in the middle.
With an even count, the median is the average of the TWO middle values. In an ordered list of 6, those are the 3rd and 4th.
The list is already ordered. Step 1: circle the 3rd and 4th values. Step 2: add them and divide by 2 — that result is the median.
approaching.stemEs: Conjunto de datos: 4, 6, 6, 8, 10, 12. ¿Cuál es la mediana?
approaching.explanationEs: Con 6 valores, la mediana es el promedio del 3.º y el 4.º valor: (6 + 8) ÷ 2 = 7.
hintsEs: Cuenta los valores: hay 6, un número par, así que ningún valor queda exactamente en el medio.
Con una cantidad par, la mediana es el promedio de los DOS valores centrales. En una lista ordenada de 6, esos son el 3.º y el 4.º.
La lista ya está ordenada. Paso 1: encierra el 3.º y el 4.º valor. Paso 2: súmalos y divide entre 2; ese resultado es la mediana.

onLevel.title: The Even-Count Median Mistake

workedExample.label: Data set
workedExample.work: Points per game, in order: 3, 8, 10, 14, 16, 20 (6 values)
workedExample.workEs: Puntos por partido, en orden: 3, 8, 10, 14, 16, 20 (6 valores)

workedExample.label: Goal
workedExample.work: Find the MEDIAN number of points.
workedExample.workEs: Encuentra la MEDIANA de los puntos.

workedExample.label: Pick the middle
workedExample.work: With 6 values the student grabs a single middle number and says median = 10.
workedExample.workEs: Con 6 valores, el estudiante toma un solo número del medio y dice mediana = 10.

onLevel.correctWork: When a data set has an EVEN number of values there is no single middle number. You must average the TWO middle values. Here the 3rd and 4th values are 10 and 14, so the median = (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12, not 10.
hints: With an even number of values, there are two numbers in the middle — average them.
The two middle values are 10 and 14: (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12.
onLevel.titleEs: El error de la mediana con cantidad par
onLevel.explanation: With 6 values there is no single number sitting in the middle — positions 3 and 4 tie for the center. The 3rd and 4th values are 10 and 14, so the median is their average, (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12, not just the lower one.
onLevel.explanationEs: Con 6 valores no hay un solo número en el centro: las posiciones 3 y 4 empatan en el medio. El 3.º y el 4.º valor son 10 y 14, así que la mediana es su promedio, (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12, y no solo el menor de los dos.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Cuando un conjunto de datos tiene una cantidad PAR de valores, no hay un solo número del medio. Debes promediar los DOS valores centrales. Aquí el 3.º y el 4.º son 10 y 14, así que la mediana = (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12, no 10.
hintsEs: Con un número par de valores hay dos números en el medio — sácales el promedio.
Los dos valores del medio son 10 y 14: (10 + 14) ÷ 2 = 12.

Add all five scores together first, then divide by how many quarters there were.
Start the sum: 4 + 8 + 6 + 10 + 2. Once you have that total, divide it by 5.
hintsEs: La media es la cantidad que tendría cada cuarto si los puntos se repartieran por igual.
Suma primero los cinco puntajes y luego divide entre la cantidad de cuartos.
Empieza la suma: 4 + 8 + 6 + 10 + 2. Cuando tengas ese total, divídelo entre 5.

onLevel.stem: A goalie made 3, 7, 9, 2, and 5 saves in five games. What is the MEDIAN number of saves?
onLevel.explanation: Order the saves first: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9. The middle (3rd) value is 5, so the median is 5.
choiceFeedback: The highest value is 9—is median always the maximum?
List them in order first—then count to the middle.
The smallest value is 2—is the median always the smallest?
onLevel.stemEs: Un portero hizo 3, 7, 9, 2 y 5 atajadas en cinco partidos. ¿Cuál es la MEDIANA de atajadas?
onLevel.explanationEs: Ordena primero las atajadas: 2, 3, 5, 7, 9. El valor del medio (el 3.º) es 5, así que la mediana es 5.
hints: The median is the value sitting in the middle once the data is in order.
Put the five save counts in order from least to greatest before you look for a middle.
In order they start 2, 3, ... — finish the ordering, then count in from both ends to find the value in the exact middle.
hintsEs: La mediana es el valor que queda en el medio una vez que los datos están ordenados.
Ordena las cinco cantidades de atajadas de menor a mayor antes de buscar el valor del medio.

onLevel.stem: A team scored 4, 4, 7, and 9 goals in four matches. What is the MODE?
onLevel.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often. 4 shows up twice; every other value appears once. So the mode is 4.
choiceFeedback: 7 appears once—which number appears most often?
9 appears once—which number shows up more than once?
6 is the mean—is mean the same as mode?
onLevel.stemEs: Un equipo anotó 4, 4, 7 y 9 goles en cuatro partidos. ¿Cuál es la MODA?
onLevel.explanationEs: La moda es el valor que aparece con más frecuencia. El 4 aparece dos veces; los demás valores aparecen una vez. Así que la moda es 4.
hints: The mode is the value that shows up most often in a data set.
Count how many times each number appears instead of adding or averaging.
Go through 4, 4, 7, 9 and tally each value. The number with the largest tally is the mode.
hintsEs: La moda es el valor que aparece con más frecuencia en un conjunto de datos.
Cuenta cuántas veces aparece cada número en lugar de sumar o promediar.
Recorre 4, 4, 7, 9 y anota cuántas veces sale cada valor. El número con la mayor cuenta es la moda.

onLevel.stem: One game was a 55-point outlier. Which measure of center best shows a TYPICAL game?
choices: The median, because the outlier barely moves the middle value
The mean, because it uses every score
The mode, because it is always the typical value
The range, because it shows the spread
onLevel.explanation: A high outlier pulls the mean upward, making it larger than most games. The median is the middle of the ordered data, so one unusual game barely changes it — it best describes a typical game.
choiceFeedback: The mean is pulled higher by the outlier—how does the median respond?
Mode is the most common value—does it handle outliers better than mean?
Range is 53—does range show a typical game?
onLevel.stemEs: Un partido fue un valor atípico de 55 puntos. ¿Cuál medida de centro muestra mejor un partido TÍPICO?
onLevel.explanationEs: Un valor atípico alto jala la media hacia arriba y la hace mayor que la mayoría de los partidos. La mediana es el centro de los datos ordenados, así que un partido inusual casi no la cambia: describe mejor un partido típico.
hints: An outlier is a value that sits far away from the rest of the data.
Think about which measure reacts to one huge number: the one built from a total, or the one built from position in the ordered list?
Picture replacing an ordinary score with 55. Recompute what happens to the total, then ask whether the middle value moved at all.
hintsEs: Un valor atípico es un valor que queda muy lejos del resto de los datos.
Piensa en cuál medida reacciona ante un número enorme: ¿la que se construye con una suma total o la que se construye con la posición en la lista ordenada?
Imagina que cambias un puntaje normal por 55. Vuelve a calcular qué le pasa al total y luego pregúntate si el valor del medio se movió.
choicesEs: La mediana, porque el valor atípico casi no mueve el valor del medio
La media, porque usa todos los puntajes
La moda, porque siempre es el valor típico
El rango, porque muestra la dispersión

onLevel.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — El error de la mediana
onLevel.explanation: The 7 sits in the middle of the list as written, but the list was never sorted. Ordered least to greatest the data is 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, so the true third value — and the median — is 6.
onLevel.explanationEs: El 7 está en el centro de la lista tal como está escrita, pero la lista nunca se ordenó. Ordenada de menor a mayor, los datos son 2, 4, 6, 7, 9, así que el verdadero tercer valor —y la mediana— es 6.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Debes ORDENAR los datos antes de buscar el del medio. Ordenados de menor a mayor: 2, 4, 6, 7, 9. El verdadero valor del medio (el 3.º) es 6, así que la mediana = 6, no 7.
hintsEs: La mediana es el medio de los datos SOLO después de ordenarlos de menor a mayor.
Reordena 9, 4, 7, 2, 6 → 2, 4, 6, 7, 9. Ahora halla el valor del medio.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Mean, Median, and Mode is finding the median without ordering the data first — students pick the middle number straight from the list as given (for 9, 4, 7, 2, 6 they say the median is 7, the middle position in that original order) instead of sorting least to greatest (2, 4, 6, 7, 9) and finding the true middle value, 6. Before finalizing a median, always reorder the data smallest to largest, then count to the middle position — and if there is an even number of values, average the two middle numbers.

optionalActivity.name: Sports Stats Center: Mean, Median, Mode
optionalActivity.intro: Optional — one more together if the group is ready: Crunch the team's numbers to find the center of the data and prove which stat tells the real story.

diagram.title: Class Quiz Scores — Dot Plot
diagram.caption: The tallest stack sits at 92 — the mode. The balance point (mean) is 86.6. Both describe the center, but they land in different places.

connect.scenario: Your class took a math quiz. The scores were: 85, 92, 78, 88, 92, 95, 72, 88, 92, 84. The teacher says 'most students scored around 87.' A student disagrees and says 'the most common score was 92.'
connect.promptQuestion: Who is using the mean, and who is using the mode? Which is more useful here?
connect.prompt: The teacher used the ___ (about 86.6). The student used the ___ (92). The ___ is more useful here because ___.

check.stem: The teacher said 'most students scored around 87.' Which measure is that?
choices: The mean (average)
The mode
The median
The range
check.explanation: The mean is the balance point: 866 ÷ 10 = 86.6, which rounds to about 87.

check.stem: The student said 'the most common score was 92.' Which measure is that?
choices: The mode
The mean
The median
The range
check.explanation: The mode is the value that appears most often. 92 shows up three times — more than any other score.

check.stem: What is the median of the 10 scores?
check.explanation: In order: 72, 78, 84, 85, 88, 88, 92, 92, 92, 95. With 10 values the median is the average of the 5th and 6th: (88 + 88) ÷ 2 = 88.

connect.modelAnswer: The teacher used the MEAN: 866 ÷ 10 = 86.6, about 87. The student used the MODE: 92 appears three times, more than any other score. Both are correct measures of center — they simply answer different questions. The mean is the balance point of all the scores; the mode is the single most common score.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: Data set: 4, 7, 10, 7, 12. What is the median, and what does it tell you?
choices: 7 — a typical value in this set is about 7
10 — it is the middle number as the list is written
8 — it is the average of all five values
12 — it is the largest value
exitTicket.explanation: Put the values in order first: 4, 7, 7, 10, 12. With five values the middle is the 3rd, so the median is 7 — half the values sit at or below it.
choiceFeedback: That takes the middle of the UNORDERED list. The data must be ordered before a middle means anything.
That is the mean, a different measure of center. The median is a position, not a total shared out.
The largest value is the maximum, not the middle.
hints: Order the five values from least to greatest first.
With five values, which position is the middle?
Count in from both ends until one value is left.

revealSlides.caption: Notice & Wonder — what do you notice about the teaching-experience data?
How can you organize the values to find the middle?
The values in order — what does it mean to be in the middle?
Math is Applying — find the median another way.
Collaborate & Connect — the same data on a dot plot.
Worked summary — the median describes the data set.
More teachers join the data — how does the median change?
An even number of values — the median is halfway between the middle two.
Learning targets — can you do these now?

questions.stem: Which question is NOT a statistical question?
choices: How many home runs did each player hit this year?
How many innings are in a baseball game?
How many miles does each runner train per week?
How tall is each player on the basketball team?
questions.explanation: "How many innings are in a baseball game?" has one fixed answer (9) — no variability. The other questions all produce different answers for different people.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a statistical question?
choices: How many points are scored for a free throw?
How many points did each player score this season?
What sport does this team play?
How many halves are in a soccer game?
questions.explanation: "How many points did each player score?" is statistical because different players will have different scores — there is variability in the data.

questions.stem: Why is 'How many hours of sleep did each student get last night?' a statistical question?
choices: Because it asks about sleep
Because hours are numbers
Because the answer is always 8 hours
Because different students got different amounts of sleep
questions.explanation: A statistical question anticipates variability — different students slept different amounts, so the data will vary.
